+"""End-to-end tests for `sith.py complete`."""

+import json

+import os

+import subprocess

+import sys

+import tempfile

+import unittest

+

+SITH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "sith.py")

+

+

+def dedent(source):

+    """Like textwrap.dedent, but keeps the indentation of whitespace-only lines."""

+    lines = source.split("\n")

+    indents = [len(l) - len(l.lstrip()) for l in lines if l.strip()]

+    margin = min(indents) if indents else 0

+    return "\n".join(l[min(margin, len(l) - len(l.lstrip())):] for l in lines)

+

+

+class SithTestCase(unittest.TestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

+        self.dir = self._tmp.name

+

+    def tearDown(self):

+        self._tmp.cleanup()

+

+    def write(self, name, source):

+        path = os.path.join(self.dir, name)

+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)

+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:

+            handle.write(dedent(source))

+        return path

+

+    def run_sith(self, *args):

+        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SITH, "complete", *map(str, args)],

+                              capture_output=True, text=True)

+

+    def complete(self, source, line, col, *flags, name="main.py"):

+        path = self.write(name, source)

+        result = self.run_sith(path, line, col, *flags)

+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)

+        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.endswith("\n"))

+        self.assertNotIn(" ", result.stdout.split('"description"')[0].replace('" ', ""))

+        return json.loads(result.stdout)["completions"]

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def by_name(completions):

+        return {c["name"]: c for c in completions}

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def names(completions, include_keywords=True):

+        return [c["name"] for c in completions if include_keywords or c["type"] != "keyword"]

+

+

+class NameCompletionTests(SithTestCase):

+    def test_builtin_prefix(self):

+        result = self.by_name(self.complete("pr", 1, 2))

+        self.assertEqual(result["print"], {"name": "print", "complete": "int", "type": "function",

+                                           "description": "def print(...)"})

+        self.assertEqual(result["property"]["description"], "class property")

+        self.assertEqual(result["property"]["complete"], "operty")

+

+    def test_case_insensitive_complete_by_length(self):

+        result = self.by_name(self.complete("PRI", 1, 3))

+        self.assertEqual(result["print"]["complete"], "nt")

+

+    def test_scopes_and_visibility(self):

+        source = "\n".join([

+            "import os",

+            "GLOBAL = 1",

+            "def outer(p, q=3):",

+            "    local = [1]",

+            "    def inner():",

+            "        z = 1",

+            "        ",

+            "    return inner",

+            "LATER = 2",

+        ])

+        result = self.by_name(self.complete(source, 7, 8))

+        for name in ("z", "local", "p", "q", "inner", "outer", "GLOBAL", "os", "print"):

+            self.assertIn(name, result)

+        self.assertNotIn("LATER", result)

+        self.assertEqual(result["p"]["type"], "param")

+        self.assertEqual(result["os"]["description"], "module os")

+        self.assertEqual(result["local"]["description"], "instance of list")

+

+    def test_not_visible_before_definition(self):

+        source = "a = 1\n\nb = 2\n"

+        names = self.names(self.complete(source, 2, 0))

+        self.assertIn("a", names)

+        self.assertNotIn("b", names)

+        source = "_priv = 1\n__dund__ = 2\nZeta = 3\nalpha = 4\n\n"

+        self.assertEqual(keywords, sorted(keywords, key=str.lower))

+

+    def test_keywords_included(self):

+        result = self.by_name(self.complete("wh", 1, 2))

+        self.assertEqual(result["while"], {"name": "while", "complete": "ile", "type": "keyword",

+

+    def test_fuzzy(self):

+        names = self.names(self.complete("isins", 1, 5))

+        self.assertIn("isinstance", names)

+        self.assertIn("isinstance", names)

+"""Textual analysis of the cursor position: prefix and completion kind."""

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+

+NAME = "name"

+ATTRIBUTE = "attribute"

+NONE = "none"

+

+_OPENERS = {")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{"}

+_STRING_PREFIX_CHARS = "rRbBuUfF"

+

+

+@dataclass

+class CursorContext:

+    """What kind of completion is requested and what has been typed so far."""

+

+    kind: str

+    prefix: str = ""

+    receiver: str = ""

+

+

+def is_identifier_char(char):

+    return char == "_" or char.isalnum()

+

+

+def analyze(text_before_cursor):

+    """Classify the completion request from the source text before the cursor."""

+    end = len(text_before_cursor)

+    start = end

+    while start > 0 and is_identifier_char(text_before_cursor[start - 1]):

+        start -= 1

+    prefix = text_before_cursor[start:]

+    if prefix and prefix[0].isdigit():

+        return CursorContext(NONE, prefix)

+

+    before = text_before_cursor[:start]

+    if not before.endswith("."):

+        return CursorContext(NAME, prefix)

+

+    receiver = extract_receiver(before[:-1])

+    if not receiver or receiver.isdigit() or receiver.endswith("."):

+        return CursorContext(NONE, prefix)

+    return CursorContext(ATTRIBUTE, prefix, receiver)

+

+

+def extract_receiver(text):

+    """Return the expression text that ends at the end of `text`, or None."""

+    i = len(text)

+    while i > 0:

+        char = text[i - 1]

+        if char in _OPENERS:

+            opener = _match_open(text, i - 1)

+            if opener is None:

+                return None

+            i = opener

+            continue

+        if is_identifier_char(char):

+            while i > 0 and is_identifier_char(text[i - 1]):

+                i -= 1

+            if i > 0 and text[i - 1] == ".":

+                i -= 1

+                continue

+            break

+        if char in "\"'":

+            start = _string_start(text, i - 1)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            i = start

+            while i > 0 and text[i - 1] in _STRING_PREFIX_CHARS:

+                i -= 1

+            break

+        break

+    return text[i:].strip()

+

+

+def _match_open(text, close_index):

+    """Index of the bracket opening the one at `close_index`, scanning backwards."""

+    stack = [text[close_index]]

+    i = close_index - 1

+    while i >= 0:

+        char = text[i]

+        if char in "\"'":

+            start = _string_start(text, i)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            i = start - 1

+            continue

+        if char in _OPENERS:

+            stack.append(char)

+        elif char in "([{":

+            if _OPENERS[stack[-1]] != char:

+                return None

+            stack.pop()

+            if not stack:

+                return i

+        i -= 1

+    return None

+

+

+def _string_start(text, end_index):

+    """Index of the opening quote of the string literal ending at `end_index`."""

+    quote = text[end_index]

+    if end_index >= 2 and text[end_index - 2:end_index + 1] == quote * 3:

+        start = text.rfind(quote * 3, 0, end_index - 2)

+        return None if start < 0 else start

+    i = end_index - 1

+    while i >= 0:

+        if text[i] == quote and (i == 0 or text[i - 1] != "\\"):

+            return i

+        if text[i] == "\n":

+            return None

+        i -= 1

+    return None

+"""Lazily-described completion candidates.

+

+An entry stands for whatever a name refers to; its value and description are

+only computed when the name survives prefix filtering.

+"""

+from .describe import (

+    describe_class,

+    describe_function,

+    describe_module,

+    describe_param,

+    describe_value,

+)

+

+_UNSET = object()

+

+

+class BindingEntry:

+    """A name bound by a statement in parsed source."""

+

+    def __init__(self, binding, inferrer):

+        self.binding = binding

+        self.inferrer = inferrer

+

+    def value(self):

+        return self.inferrer.infer_binding(self.binding)

+

+    def describe(self, name):

+        kind = self.binding.kind

+        if kind == "param":

+            return describe_param(name)

+        if kind == "def":

+            return describe_function(name)

+        if kind == "class":

+            return describe_class(name)

+        if kind == "import":

+            return describe_module(name)

+        return describe_value(name, self.value())

+

+

+class ValueEntry:

+    """A name whose value is produced on demand by a factory."""

+

+    def __init__(self, factory):

+        self._factory = factory

+        self._value = _UNSET

+

+    def value(self):

+        if self._value is _UNSET:

+            try:

+                self._value = self._factory()

+            except Exception:

+                self._value = None

+        return self._value

+

+    def describe(self, name):

+        return describe_value(name, self.value())

+"""Finding the innermost scope that contains the cursor."""

+import ast

+

+from .scopes import COMPREHENSION, LAMBDA

+

+_DEFINITIONS = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)

+

+

+def cursor_indent(line_text, col):

+    """Indentation that governs the cursor's block membership."""

+    before = line_text[:col]

+    if not before.strip():

+        return len(before)

+    return len(line_text) - len(line_text.lstrip())

+

+

+def find_scope(context, line, col, line_text):

+    """The innermost Scope of `context` enclosing the cursor at (line, col)."""

+    byte_col = len(line_text[:col].encode("utf-8"))

+    indent = cursor_indent(line_text, col)

+    scope = context.root

+    for node in _definition_chain(context.tree.body, line, byte_col, indent):

+        scope = context.scope_of(node) or scope

+    return _innermost_expression_scope(scope, line, byte_col)

+

+

+def _definition_chain(statements, line, byte_col, indent):

+    """def/class nodes whose bodies contain the cursor, outermost first."""

+    chain = []

+    while True:

+        candidate = None

+        for statement in statements:

+            if statement.lineno <= line:

+                candidate = statement

+            else:

+                break

+        if candidate is None:

+            return chain

+        inside = line <= candidate.end_lineno or indent > candidate.col_offset

+        if not inside:

+            return chain

+        if isinstance(candidate, _DEFINITIONS):

+            if not _in_body(candidate, line, byte_col):

+                return chain

+            chain.append(candidate)

+            statements = candidate.body

+        else:

+            statements = _child_statements(candidate)

+            if not statements:

+                return chain

+

+

+def _in_body(node, line, byte_col):

+    first = node.body[0]

+    if line > _header_end(node):

+        return True

+    return line == first.lineno and byte_col >= first.col_offset

+

+

+def _header_end(node):

+    parts = []

+    if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):

+        parts = node.bases + [k.value for k in node.keywords]

+    else:

+        args = node.args

+        parts = args.posonlyargs + args.args + args.kwonlyargs + args.defaults

+        parts += [d for d in args.kw_defaults if d is not None]

+        parts += [a for a in (args.vararg, args.kwarg, node.returns) if a is not None]

+    return max([node.lineno] + [getattr(p, "end_lineno", None) or node.lineno for p in parts])

+

+

+def _child_statements(node):

+    children = []

+    for field in ("body", "orelse", "finalbody"):

+        children += [s for s in getattr(node, field, []) if isinstance(s, ast.stmt)]

+    for handler in getattr(node, "handlers", []):

+        children += handler.body

+    for case in getattr(node, "cases", []):

+        children += case.body

+    return sorted(children, key=lambda s: (s.lineno, s.col_offset))

+

+

+def _contains(node, line, byte_col):

+    start = (node.lineno, node.col_offset)

+    end = (node.end_lineno, node.end_col_offset)

+    return start <= (line, byte_col) <= end

+

+

+def _innermost_expression_scope(scope, line, byte_col):

+    """Descend into lambda/comprehension scopes that contain the cursor."""

+    while True:

+        for child in scope.children:

+            if child.kind in (LAMBDA, COMPREHENSION) and _contains(child.node, line, byte_col):

+                scope = child

+                break

+        else:

+            return scope

+def builtin_entries():

+    """Entries for every name in the `builtins` module.

+

+    Names that are also keywords (True, False, None) are offered only as

+    keywords, so they are left out here.

+"""Error-tolerant parsing of Python source into an AST.

+

+Syntax errors are repaired line by line: the offending line is replaced by a

+sequence of progressively more conservative candidates (a placeholder name at

+the cursor, `pass`, and finally a blank line) until the module parses.  Lines

+are never inserted or removed, so AST line numbers match the original file.

+"""

+import ast

+import re

+import time

+import warnings

+

+# Identifier inserted at the cursor to make incomplete expressions parseable.

+# Bindings whose names contain it are ignored by scope analysis.

+PLACEHOLDER = "__sith_cursor__"

+

+# After this many seconds of repairs, everything from the error onward is dropped.

+_TIME_BUDGET = 1.0

+_INDENTATION_ERRORS = ("unindent does not match", "unexpected indent")

+_INDENTED_BLOCK = re.compile(r"expected an indented block after .* on line (\d+)")

+

+_CLOSERS = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}

+# Keywords that can never appear inside a bracketed expression.

+_STATEMENT_KEYWORDS = {

+    "def", "class", "return", "import", "pass", "break", "continue", "raise", "del",

+    "global", "nonlocal", "assert", "while", "with", "try", "except", "finally", "elif",

+}

+# Keywords that, at or below the opening line's indentation, start a new statement.

+_BLOCK_KEYWORDS = {"if", "for", "else", "async", "from", "match", "case"}

+_FIRST_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*")

+

+

+def parse_tolerant(text, cursor=None):

+    """Parse `text`, repairing syntax errors. `cursor` is (line, col) or None."""

+    lines = close_brackets(text.replace("\0", " ").split("\n"))

+    return _Repairer(lines, cursor).run()

+

+

+def close_brackets(lines):

+    """Close brackets left open when a new statement evidently begins.

+

+    An unclosed bracket otherwise swallows every following line, and the

+    parser then blames those (valid) lines instead of the incomplete one.

+    """

+    lines = list(lines)

+    stack = []  # (bracket, line index)

+    triple = None

+    for index, line in enumerate(lines):

+        if stack and triple is None and _starts_statement(line, lines[stack[0][1]]):

+            _append_closers(lines, stack, index)

+        triple = _scan_brackets(line, stack, triple, index)

+    if stack and triple is None:

+        _append_closers(lines, stack, len(lines))

+    return lines

+

+

+def _starts_statement(line, opener_line):

+    code = line.strip()

+    if not code or code.startswith("#"):

+        return False

+    indent = len(_indent_of(line))

+    opener_indent = len(_indent_of(opener_line))

+    match = _FIRST_WORD.match(code)

+    word = match.group(0) if match else ""

+    if word in _STATEMENT_KEYWORDS:

+        return True

+    if indent <= opener_indent and (word in _BLOCK_KEYWORDS or code.startswith("@")):

+        return True

+    return indent < opener_indent and code[0] not in ")]}"

+

+

+def _append_closers(lines, stack, before):

+    """Append closers for `stack` to the last code line before index `before`."""

+    for index in range(before - 1, stack[0][1] - 1, -1):

+        code = strip_comment(lines[index]).rstrip()

+        if code.strip():

+            lines[index] = code + "".join(_CLOSERS[b] for b, _ in reversed(stack))

+            break

+    stack.clear()

+

+

+def _scan_brackets(line, stack, triple, index):

+    """Update the bracket stack with `line`; returns the open triple quote, if any."""

+    i = 0

+    while i < len(line):

+        if triple is not None:

+            end = line.find(triple, i)

+            if end < 0:

+            i = end + 3

+            triple = None

+            continue

+        char = line[i]

+        if char == "#":

+            break

+        if char in "\"'":

+            if line.startswith(char * 3, i):

+                triple = char * 3

+                i += 3

+                continue

+            i += 1

+            while i < len(line) and line[i] != char:

+                i += 2 if line[i] == "\\" else 1

+        elif char in _CLOSERS:

+            stack.append((char, index))

+        elif char in ")]}" and stack and _CLOSERS[stack[-1][0]] == char:

+            stack.pop()

+    return triple

+def strip_comment(line):

+    """Remove a trailing `#` comment, ignoring `#` inside string literals."""

+    quote = None

+    i = 0

+    while i < len(line):

+        char = line[i]

+        if quote:

+            if char == "\\":

+                i += 1

+            elif char == quote:

+                quote = None

+        elif char in "\"'":

+        elif char == "#":

+        i += 1

+def _neighbour_indent(lines):

+    for line in lines:

+            return len(_indent_of(line))

+def _indent_of(line):

+    return line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]

+class _Repairer:

+    def __init__(self, lines, cursor):

+        self.state = list(lines)

+        self.cursor = cursor

+        self.truncated = False

+        self.deadline = time.monotonic() + _TIME_BUDGET

+            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

+                    if not self._repair(error):

+        count = len(self.state)

+        line = getattr(error, "lineno", None) or count

+        line = max(1, min(line, count))

+        message = str(getattr(error, "msg", ""))

+        if not self.truncated and time.monotonic() > self.deadline:

+            self._drop_from(line)

+            return True

+        match = _INDENTED_BLOCK.search(message)

+        if match:

+            if self._is_cursor_line(line) and self._advance(line):

+                return True

+            if self._append_pass(int(match.group(1)), line):

+                return True

+        if any(text in message for text in _INDENTATION_ERRORS) and self._blank(line):

+            return True

+        if self._advance(line):

+            return True

+        for previous in range(line - 1, 0, -1):

+            if self._advance(previous):

+                return True

+        return False

+

+    def _is_cursor_line(self, line):

+        return self.cursor is not None and self.cursor[0] == line

+

+    def _drop_from(self, line):

+        """Give up on the rest of the file: blank every line from `line` on."""

+        for index in range(line - 1, len(self.state)):

+            self.state[index] = ""

+            self._line_candidates(index + 1)

+            self.positions[index + 1] = len(self.candidates[index + 1]) - 1

+        self.truncated = True

+

+    def _blank(self, line):

+        """Jump straight to the blank candidate (indentation cannot be fixed in place)."""

+        options = self._line_candidates(line)

+        if self.state[line - 1] == "":

+            return False

+        self.positions[line] = len(options) - 1

+        self.state[line - 1] = ""

+        return True

+

+    def _close_string(self, error, line):

+        """Terminate a triple-quoted string that runs to the end of the file."""

+        offset = (getattr(error, "offset", None) or 1) - 1

+        quote = self.state[line - 1][offset:offset + 3]

+        if quote not in ('"""', "'''") or self.string_closed:

+            return False

+        self.state[-1] += " " + quote

+        self.string_closed = True

+        return True

+

+    def _append_pass(self, header_line, error_line):

+        """Give a block header with a missing body an inline `pass` body."""

+        last = min(max(error_line, header_line), len(self.state))

+        for line in range(last, header_line - 1, -1):

+            code = strip_comment(self.state[line - 1]).rstrip()

+            if code.endswith(":") and line not in self.pass_appended:

+                self.state[line - 1] = code + " pass"

+                self.pass_appended.add(line)

+                return True

+        return False

+

+    def _line_candidates(self, line):

+        if line not in self.candidates:

+            text = self.original[line - 1]

+            indent = _indent_of(text)

+            options = [text]

+            if self._is_cursor_line(line):

+                col = min(self.cursor[1], len(text))

+                options.append(text[:col] + PLACEHOLDER + text[col:])

+                options.append(text[:col] + PLACEHOLDER)

+            if self._out_of_place(line, text):

+                options.append("")

+            header = self._header_replacement(line, text)

+            if header:

+                options.append(header)

+            options += [indent + "pass", ""]

+            unique = []

+            for option in options:

+                if option not in unique:

+                    unique.append(option)

+            self.candidates[line] = unique

+            self.positions[line] = 0

+        return self.candidates[line]

+

+    def _out_of_place(self, line, text):

+        """True for a line dedented below both its neighbouring code lines."""

+        indent = len(_indent_of(text))

+        before = _neighbour_indent(reversed(self.original[: line - 1]))

+        after = _neighbour_indent(self.original[line:])

+        return before is not None and after is not None and indent < min(before, after)

+

+    def _header_replacement(self, line, text):

+        """A valid block header for a broken line that is followed by a block.

+

+        Keeping a header lets the indented body that follows still parse,

+        instead of failing line by line with "unexpected indent".

+        """

+        indent = _indent_of(text)

+        for following in self.original[line:]:

+            if following.strip() and not following.strip().startswith("#"):

+                if len(_indent_of(following)) <= len(indent):

+                    return None

+                break

+        else:

+            return None

+        word = (_FIRST_WORD.match(text.strip()) or [""])[0]

+        if word in ("def", "async"):

+            return f"{indent}def {PLACEHOLDER}():"

+        if word == "class":

+            return f"{indent}class {PLACEHOLDER}:"

+        return f"{indent}if True:"

+

+    def _advance(self, line):

+        """Switch `line` to its next repair candidate; False when exhausted."""

+        options = self._line_candidates(line)

+        position = self.positions[line]

+        while position + 1 < len(options):

+            position += 1

+            if options[position] != self.state[line - 1]:

+                self.positions[line] = position

+                self.state[line - 1] = options[position]

+                return True

+        self.positions[line] = position

+        return False

+

+    @property

+    kind = CLASS

+

+    def __init__(self, obj):

+        self.obj = obj

+

+

+class RuntimeFunction(Value):

+    kind = FUNCTION

+

+    def __init__(self, obj):

+        self.obj = obj

+

+

+class RuntimeInstance(Value):

+    """An instance of a runtime class (also used for literals)."""

+

+    kind = INSTANCE

+

+    def __init__(self, cls):

+        self.cls = cls

+

+    @property

+    def type_name(self):

+        return self.cls.__name__

+def wrap_runtime(obj):

+    """Wrap a live Python object as a Value (None for opaque data descriptors)."""

+    if inspect.ismodule(obj):

+"""Loading source documents and validating cursor positions."""

+import os

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+

+from .errors import SithError

+

+

+@dataclass

+class Document:

+    """A source file split into lines, with cursor-related helpers."""

+

+    path: str

+    text: str

+    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)

+

+    @property

+    def directory(self):

+        return os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))

+

+    def check_position(self, line, col):

+        """Validate a 1-based line and 0-based column."""

+        if line < 1 or line > len(self.lines):

+            raise SithError(f"line {line} is out of range (file has {len(self.lines)} lines)")

+        length = len(self.lines[line - 1])

+        if col < 0 or col > length:

+            raise SithError(f"column {col} is out of range (line {line} has {length} characters)")

+

+    def text_before(self, line, col):

+        """All source text preceding the cursor."""

+        return "\n".join(self.lines[: line - 1] + [self.lines[line - 1][:col]])

+

+

+def normalize_newlines(text):

+    return text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

+

+

+def read_text(path):

+    """Read a file as UTF-8 text, raising SithError on any problem."""

+    if not os.path.exists(path):

+        raise SithError(f"file not found: {path}")

+    if not os.path.isfile(path):

+        raise SithError(f"not a regular file: {path}")

+    try:

+        with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+            raw = handle.read()

+    except OSError as exc:

+        raise SithError(f"cannot read {path}: {exc}") from exc

+    try:

+        text = raw.decode("utf-8")

+    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:

+        raise SithError(f"file is not valid UTF-8: {path}") from exc

+    if text.startswith("\ufeff"):

+        text = text[1:]

+    return normalize_newlines(text)

+

+

+def load_document(path):

+    text = read_text(path)

+    return Document(path=path, text=text, lines=text.split("\n"))

+            return RuntimeInstance(type(node.value))

+        literal = _LITERAL_TYPES.get(type(node))

+        if literal is not None:

+            return RuntimeInstance(literal)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Name):

+            entry = self.lookup(node.id, scope, line, strict)

+            return entry.value() if entry is not None else None

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):

+            base = self.infer(node.value, scope, line, strict)

+            return self.members.member(base, node.attr) if base is not None else None

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):

+            return self._infer_call(node, scope, line, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Lambda):

+            lambda_scope = scope.module.scope_of(node)

+            return LocalFunction(lambda_scope) if lambda_scope else None

+        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):

+            return self._infer_binop(node, scope, line, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):

+            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not):

+                return RuntimeInstance(bool)

+            return self.infer(node.operand, scope, line, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.IfExp):

+            return self.infer(node.body, scope, line, strict) or self.infer(

+                node.orelse, scope, line, strict)

+        if isinstance(node, ast.NamedExpr):

+            return self.infer(node.value, scope, line, strict)

+        return None

+

+    def _infer_call(self, node, scope, line, strict):

+        function = self.infer(node.func, scope, line, strict)

+        if function is None:

+            return None

+        if isinstance(function, (LocalClass, RuntimeClass)):

+            return instance_of(function)

+        if isinstance(function, LocalFunction):

+            return self.infer_return(function)

+        return None

+

+    def _infer_binop(self, node, scope, line, strict):

+        left = self.infer(node.left, scope, line, strict)

+        if not isinstance(left, RuntimeInstance):

+            return None

+        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mod) and left.cls in (str, bytes):

+            return left

+        right = self.infer(node.right, scope, line, strict)

+        if isinstance(right, RuntimeInstance) and right.cls is left.cls:

+            return left

+        return None

+

+    def infer_return(self, function):

+        """The value returned by calling a locally defined function."""

+        scope = function.scope

+        node = scope.node

+        key = ("return", id(node))

+        if key in self._active:

+            return None

+        self._active.add(key)

+        try:

+            if isinstance(node, ast.Lambda):

+                return self.infer(node.body, scope, node.lineno)

+            if isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef):

+                return None

+            returns = []

+            for child in walk_local(node.body):

+                if isinstance(child, (ast.Yield, ast.YieldFrom)):

+                    return RuntimeInstance(types.GeneratorType)

+                if isinstance(child, ast.Return) and child.value is not None:

+                    returns.append(child)

+            for statement in returns:

+                value = self.infer(statement.value, scope, statement.lineno)

+                if value is not None:

+                    return value

+            return None

+        finally:

+            self._active.discard(key)

+

+

+def _latest_binding(bindings, limit):

+    """The binding in effect at line `limit` (any line when `limit` is None).

+

+    A binding on the limit line itself (e.g. `x = x + 1`, or the statement

+    being typed) only counts when there is no earlier one.

+    """

+    if limit is None:

+        pool = bindings

+    else:

+        pool = [b for b in bindings if b.line < limit] or [b for b in bindings if b.line == limit]

+    if not pool:

+        return None

+    return max(enumerate(pool), key=lambda pair: (pair[1].line, pair[0]))[1]

+

+

+def _default_for(arguments, arg):

+    positional = arguments.posonlyargs + arguments.args

+    if arg in positional:

+        offset = len(positional) - len(arguments.defaults)

+        index = positional.index(arg)

+        return arguments.defaults[index - offset] if index >= offset else None

+    if arg in arguments.kwonlyargs:

+        return arguments.kw_defaults[arguments.kwonlyargs.index(arg)]

+    return None

+

+

+def _decorator_name(node):

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):

+        node = node.func

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):

+        return node.attr

+    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):

+        return node.id

+    return None

+

+"""Scope analysis: which names each scope binds, and where."""

+import ast

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+

+from .parsing import PLACEHOLDER

+

+MODULE = "module"

+FUNCTION = "function"

+CLASS = "class"

+LAMBDA = "lambda"

+COMPREHENSION = "comprehension"

+

+_FUNCTION_NODES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)

+_COMPREHENSION_NODES = (ast.ListComp, ast.SetComp, ast.DictComp, ast.GeneratorExp)

+

+

+@dataclass(eq=False)

+class Binding:

+    """A single place where a name is bound."""

+

+    name: str

+    line: int

+    kind: str

+    node: ast.AST

+    scope: "Scope"

+    value: ast.AST = None

+    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

+

+@dataclass(eq=False)

+class StarImport:

+    """A `from module import *` statement."""

+

+    module: str

+    level: int

+    line: int

+    scope: "Scope"

+

+class Scope:

+    """A namespace: module, function, class, lambda or comprehension."""

+

+    def __init__(self, kind, node, parent, module):

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.node = node

+        self.parent = parent

+        self.module = module

+        self.bindings = {}

+        self.star_imports = []

+        self.children = []

+        self.global_names = set()

+        self.nonlocal_names = set()

+        if parent is not None:

+            parent.children.append(self)

+    def add(self, binding):

+        self.bindings.setdefault(binding.name, []).append(binding)

+

+    def chain(self):

+        scope = self

+        while scope is not None:

+            yield scope

+            scope = scope.parent

+

+    def root(self):

+        scope = self

+        while scope.parent is not None:

+            scope = scope.parent

+        return scope

+

+

+def iter_target_names(target, value):

+    """Yield (Name node, value expression or None) pairs for an assignment target."""

+    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):

+        yield target, value

+    elif isinstance(target, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)):

+        values = None

+        if (

+            isinstance(value, (ast.Tuple, ast.List))

+            and len(value.elts) == len(target.elts)

+            and not any(isinstance(e, ast.Starred) for e in target.elts + value.elts)

+    params = list(arguments.posonlyargs) + list(arguments.args)

+    if arguments.vararg:

+    params += list(arguments.kwonlyargs)

+    if arguments.kwarg:

+

+def walk_local(statements):

+    """Walk nodes of a body without descending into nested scopes."""

+    stack = list(reversed(statements))

+    while stack:

+        node = stack.pop()

+            if item.optional_vars is not None:

+            if handler.name:

+        self._statements(scope, node.finalbody)

+    _stmt_TryStar = _stmt_Try

+    def _stmt_Match(self, scope, node):

+"""The completion engine: ties context, parsing, scopes and inference together."""

+import ast

+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

+

+from . import context as cursor_context

+from .builtin_scope import KEYWORDS

+from .describe import describe_keyword

+from .inference import Inferrer

+from .locate import find_scope

+from .matching import make_matcher

+from .members import is_public

+from .modules import Importer, ModuleContext

+from .parsing import parse_tolerant

+from .ranking import sort_keywords, sort_names

+from .source import load_document

+from .values import MODULE

+

+

+@dataclass

+class Completion:

+    name: str

+    complete: str

+    type: str

+    description: str

+

+    def to_dict(self):

+        return asdict(self)

+

+

+def complete_file(path, line, col, fuzzy=False):

+    """Completions for the cursor at 1-based `line`, 0-based `col` of `path`."""

+    document = load_document(path)

+    document.check_position(line, col)

+    return Completer(document, line, col, fuzzy).run()

+

+

+class Completer:

+    def __init__(self, document, line, col, fuzzy):

+        self.document = document

+        self.line = line

+        self.col = col

+        self.fuzzy = fuzzy

+

+    def run(self):

+        request = cursor_context.analyze(self.document.text_before(self.line, self.col))

+        if request.kind == cursor_context.NONE:

+            return []

+

+        importer = Importer(self.document.directory)

+        tree = parse_tolerant(self.document.text, cursor=(self.line, self.col))

+        module = ModuleContext(self.document.path, "__main__", tree)

+        importer.register(module)

+        inferrer = Inferrer(importer)

+        scope = find_scope(module, self.line, self.col, self.document.lines[self.line - 1])

+

+        if request.kind == cursor_context.ATTRIBUTE:

+            entries = self._attribute_entries(inferrer, scope, request.receiver)

+            keywords = []

+        else:

+            entries = inferrer.visible_entries(scope, self.line)

+            keywords = KEYWORDS

+

+        matches = make_matcher(request.prefix, self.fuzzy)

+        cut = len(request.prefix)

+        results = []

+        for name in sort_names(n for n in entries if matches(n)):

+            kind, description = entries[name].describe(name)

+            results.append(Completion(name, name[cut:], kind, description))

+        for name in sort_keywords(k for k in keywords if matches(k)):

+            kind, description = describe_keyword(name)

+            results.append(Completion(name, name[cut:], kind, description))

+        return results

+

+    def _attribute_entries(self, inferrer, scope, receiver):

+        try:

+            expression = ast.parse(receiver.strip(), mode="eval").body

+        except (SyntaxError, ValueError):

+            return {}

+        value = inferrer.infer(expression, scope, self.line, strict=True)

+        if value is None:

+            return {}

+        entries = inferrer.members.all(value)

+        if value.kind == MODULE:

+            entries = {name: entry for name, entry in entries.items() if is_public(name)}

+        return entries

+                    value = node.value if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) else None

+def _self_attributes(target, value, self_name):

+        values = None

+        if isinstance(value, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)) and len(value.elts) == len(target.elts):

+            yield from _self_attributes(element, values[index] if values else None, self_name)

+    elif isinstance(target, ast.Starred):

+        yield from _self_attributes(target.value, None, self_name)

+"""Module contexts and import resolution (local files first, then installed)."""

+import contextlib

+import importlib

+import io

+import os

+import warnings

+

+from .parsing import parse_tolerant

+from .scopes import ScopeBuilder

+from .source import read_text

+from .errors import SithError

+from .values import LocalModule, RuntimeModule

+

+

+class ModuleContext:

+    """A parsed Python module together with its scope tree."""

+

+    def __init__(self, path, name, tree):

+        self.path = os.path.abspath(path) if path else None

+        self.directory = os.path.dirname(self.path) if self.path else os.getcwd()

+        self.name = name

+        self.tree = tree

+        builder = ScopeBuilder(self)

+        self.root = builder.build(tree)

+        self.scope_by_node = builder.scope_by_node

+

+    @property

+    def is_package(self):

+        return bool(self.path) and os.path.basename(self.path) == "__init__.py"

+

+    def scope_of(self, node):

+        return self.scope_by_node.get(id(node))

+

+

+class Importer:

+    """Resolves module names to values, preferring files in the project directory."""

+

+    def __init__(self, project_dir):

+        self.project_dir = project_dir

+        self._contexts = {}

+        self._runtime = {}

+

+    def register(self, context):

+        if context.path:

+            self._contexts[context.path] = context

+

+    def context_for_file(self, path, name):

+        path = os.path.abspath(path)

+        if path not in self._contexts:

+            try:

+                text = read_text(path)

+            except SithError:

+                return None

+            self._contexts[path] = ModuleContext(path, name, parse_tolerant(text))

+        return self._contexts[path]

+

+    def import_absolute(self, dotted):

+        """Resolve `import dotted` to a module value, or None."""

+        if not dotted:

+            return None

+        path = self._find_local(self.project_dir, dotted.split("."))

+        if path:

+            context = self.context_for_file(path, dotted)

+            return LocalModule(context) if context else None

+        return self._import_runtime(dotted)

+

+    def import_relative(self, context, dotted, level):

+        """Resolve `from <level dots><dotted> import ...` relative to `context`."""

+        base = context.directory

+        for _ in range(level - 1):

+            base = os.path.dirname(base)

+        parts = dotted.split(".") if dotted else []

+        path = self._find_local(base, parts) if parts else _package_init(base)

+        if not path:

+            return None

+        name = ".".join(p for p in [os.path.basename(base)] + parts if p)

+        context = self.context_for_file(path, name)

+        return LocalModule(context) if context else None

+

+    def import_module(self, context, dotted, level=0):

+        if level:

+            return self.import_relative(context, dotted, level)

+        return self.import_absolute(dotted)

+

+    def local_submodule(self, module_value, name):

+        """A submodule `name` of a local package, if such a file exists."""

+        context = module_value.context

+        if not context.is_package:

+            return None

+        path = self._find_local(context.directory, [name])

+        if not path:

+            return None

+        sub = self.context_for_file(path, f"{context.name}.{name}")

+        return LocalModule(sub) if sub else None

+

+    def runtime_submodule(self, module_value, name):

+        if not hasattr(module_value.obj, "__path__"):

+            return None

+        return self._import_runtime(f"{module_value.obj.__name__}.{name}")

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def _find_local(base, parts):

+        directory = base

+        for part in parts[:-1]:

+            directory = os.path.join(directory, part)

+            if not os.path.isdir(directory):

+                return None

+        last = os.path.join(directory, parts[-1])

+        if os.path.isfile(last + ".py"):

+            return last + ".py"

+        return _package_init(last)

+

+    def _import_runtime(self, dotted):

+        if dotted not in self._runtime:

+            module = None

+            try:

+                with warnings.catch_warnings(), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):

+                    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

+                    module = importlib.import_module(dotted)

+            except BaseException:  # importing arbitrary modules may fail in any way

+                module = None

+            self._runtime[dotted] = RuntimeModule(module) if module is not None else None

+        return self._runtime[dotted]

+

+

+def _package_init(directory):

+    init = os.path.join(directory, "__init__.py")

+    return init if os.path.isfile(init) else None

+"""Command-line interface: argument parsing, JSON output and exit codes."""

+import argparse

+import contextlib

+import io

+import json

+import sys

+

+from .completion import complete_file

+from .errors import SithError

+

+

+class _ArgumentParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):

+    """An ArgumentParser that reports usage errors as SithError (exit 1)."""

+

+    def error(self, message):

+        raise SithError(message)

+

+

+def build_parser():

+    parser = _ArgumentParser(prog="sith.py", description="Python code intelligence.")

+    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True, parser_class=_ArgumentParser)

+    complete = commands.add_parser("complete", help="complete the code at a cursor position")

+    complete.add_argument("file", help="Python source file")

+    complete.add_argument("line", type=int, help="1-based line number")

+    complete.add_argument("col", type=int, help="0-based column number")

+    complete.add_argument("--fuzzy", action="store_true", help="use fuzzy matching")

+    return parser

+

+

+def main(argv=None):

+    try:

+        args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)

+        # Introspected modules may print; keep STDOUT reserved for the JSON result.

+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):

+            completions = complete_file(args.file, args.line, args.col, fuzzy=args.fuzzy)

+    except SithError as error:

+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)

+        return 1

+    except Exception as error:  # analysis must never crash an editor integration

+        print(f"warning: analysis failed: {error!r}", file=sys.stderr)

+        completions = []

+    payload = {"completions": [c.to_dict() for c in completions]}

+    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")

+    return 0
